PockPock Agent 0.2.1 lets you report a reply that went wrong, and adds a Maintenance Manager that fixes PockPock from those reports.

## Download

| Your computer | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) | [PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe) |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) | [PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg) |
| Mac with an Intel processor | [PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg) |

**Already using 0.2.0 on Windows?** PockPock updates itself: press **Restart to update** when it appears, or check in **Settings → Updates**. On a Mac, or from 0.1.0, download and install it once, the same way as the first time. Your chats, settings and models are kept.

**New to PockPock?** Open the downloaded file, then press **Set up PockPock**; setup installs everything else. Windows may show **"Windows protected your PC"** because PockPock is not code-signed yet: press **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On a Mac, see the [installation guide](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/wiki/Installation).

## What's new

- **Report a reply.** Every reply has a **Report** button. Say what went wrong (it hung, it failed, the result was wrong) and PockPock saves that exchange with your description. Your home folder, user name, email addresses and tokens are removed first, and reports stay on your computer.
- **Maintenance page.** A new page in the sidebar lists your reports. You can open, correct or delete each one.
- **Maintenance Manager.** It works through your reports: it finds the cause in its own copy of the PockPock code, writes a fix with a documentation update, runs the checks, and shows you the change. A draft pull request is opened only after you approve it. Setup has three steps: choose the AI, connect GitHub, and allow the copy of PockPock.
- **Choose who does the fixing.**
  - **PockPock itself**, with a model on your computer, so nothing leaves it. It can optionally work through OpenClaw to run commands, build and test while fixing.
  - **Claude Code** or **GitHub Copilot**, with your own account. **Install and connect** installs the tool and opens its sign-in page for you.
- **Keep fixing reports automatically.** With this switch on, PockPock works through open reports one at a time in the background. Each fix still waits for your approval.
- **Smarter OpenClaw.** OpenClaw gets better instructions for Windows commands and for reading web pages, a turn that stops making progress is ended instead of hanging, tool errors are easier to read, and you can choose which browser it uses in **Settings**.

## Good to know

- The Maintenance Manager is new. Fixes from a small local model work best for simple problems; Claude Code and Copilot use your own plan's limits.
- The sign-in step for Claude Code and Copilot from inside PockPock, and opening a pull request after approval, have had little real-world testing. Please [report problems](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/issues/new/choose).
- The Mac versions have not been tested on a real Mac yet.
- Help, screenshots and example prompts are in the [wiki](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/wiki).
